cues.text: A treasury that keeps its own keys. A national treasury (fictional) disburses grants in a rand stablecoin. It runs the platform itself; three named officials must agree on large disbursements; an AI assistant handles small routine ones to approved recipients only.
cues.title: Government · recorded on the running platform

cues.text: Sovereign: run by the state, with no dependence on the vendor. Runs in the government’s own data centre or cloud account. FORGE supplies software and support, not custody.
cues.title: How it fits

cues.text: Three officials, set by policy. First the treasury administrator raises the approval quorum from two to three. Then the grants system asks for a large disbursement.
cues.title: Chapter 1

cues.text: The treasury administrator sets the controls.
cues.title: Sign in

cues.text: A one-time code from the person’s authenticator app. Every sign-in and every approval needs a fresh one.
cues.title: Second factor

cues.text: Raising the quorum to three approvals.
cues.title: Approval policy

cues.text: The grants system asks. A disbursement of 20 ETH to a provincial account. Policy holds it, and it now needs three officials.
cues.title: Your application

cues.text: Stored as sent, nothing signed. Three officials, none of them the requester, must approve.
cues.title: Held for three

cues.text: Three officials must agree. Each official signs in separately and approves with a fresh one-time code. Two approvals are not enough.
cues.title: Chapter 2

cues.text: A one-time code from the person’s authenticator app. Every sign-in and every approval needs a fresh one.
cues.title: Second factor

cues.text: First official: Alice.
cues.title: Approval

cues.text: A one-time code from the person’s authenticator app. Every sign-in and every approval needs a fresh one.
cues.title: Second factor

cues.text: Second official: Bob.
cues.title: Approval

cues.text: A one-time code from the person’s authenticator app. Every sign-in and every approval needs a fresh one.
cues.title: Second factor

cues.text: Two of three have approved. The request still waits; nothing is signed.
cues.title: Still waiting

cues.text: Third official: the administrator. Three of three: the stored request now runs, once.
cues.title: Approval

cues.text: Three decisions, each with who, when and how verified. Two of three signing parties signed; the chain accepted it.
cues.title: Result

cues.text: Emergency controls. Two controls that do not depend on anyone’s judgement in the moment: a list of addresses the treasury may pay, and a switch that stops everything.
cues.title: Chapter 3

cues.text: With the whitelist on, the platform refuses any destination not on it, from every route. The freeze stops all signing at once.
cues.title: Safety controls

cues.text: Every disbursement in one ledger. Records cannot be edited or deleted, by anyone, including the platform’s own database roles.
cues.title: The record

cues.text: An AI assistant for routine disbursements. Small, frequent payments, such as school-feeding grants, are delegated to an AI assistant. It may pay two approved municipalities, up to R5,000 each time.
cues.title: Chapter 4

cues.text: An agent is a credential that can only pay, within limits a person sets. It is issued here, by an admin.
cues.title: Agents

cues.text: Two approved municipalities, R5,000 a payment, R20,000 a day, fourteen days.
cues.title: Its terms

cues.text: The agent key is displayed this one time and stored only as a hash. It goes into the AI client’s secret configuration, never into a prompt. (Masked here.)
cues.title: Shown once

cues.text: Connecting an AI client. The MCP server is a small process the AI client starts. It holds only the agent key (and, for Travel Rule payments, the organisation’s own details) and calls the same gateway.
cues.title: Your application

cues.text: MCP is how AI assistants discover and call tools. The server exposes five; only one can move money, and only within the agent’s terms.
cues.title: Model Context Protocol
